target.title: fix(seo): escape JSON-LD script content to prevent breakout
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`Layout.astro` embeds structured data with
`set:html={JSON.stringify(item)}`. If any string field contains a raw
`</script>` sequence, the HTML parser closes the ld+json script element
early (classic JSON-in-script breakout).

## Evidence

Fixed escape uses a **literal** `\u003c` sequence in the serialized JSON
(not a JS string that is already `<`).

```console
$ node proof.js
layout_line: <script type="application/ld+json" set:html={JSON.stringify(item).replace(/</g, "\\u003c")} />
serialized: {"name":"\u003c/script>\u003cscript>alert(1)\u003c/script>","n":1}
contains_raw_close: false
contains_unicode_escape: true
naive_script_splits: 2
roundtrip_name: </script><script>alert(1)</script>
```

`contains_raw_close: false` means the HTML stream has no raw `</script>`
inside the JSON text. `JSON.parse` still restores the original name.

## Summary

- Escape `<` as the six-character sequence `\u003c` after `JSON.stringify`
- JS source must be `"\\u003c"` (a prior `"\u003c"` form was a no-op)

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** JSON-LD script breakout via raw less-than in stringified structured data
- **Real environment tested:** macOS, Node 22+, branch fix/json-ld-script-escape at current HEAD
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** node demo of the exact Layout expression; confirm layout line contains double-backslash escape
- **Evidence after fix:** terminal output above (no raw close sequence; roundtrip preserves name)
- **Observed result after fix:** serialized JSON cannot close the script tag early; data still parses
- **What was not tested:** full `astro build` HTML on this machine (design-system package resolution blocked in worktree); logic matches the committed Layout expression

## Related

- ClawSweeper review caught the no-op `"\u003c"` form
- React/Next JSON-LD escape guidance

target.title: fix(gateway): enforce plugin-ownership check in sessions.patch
target.body:
Closes #103077.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where an in-process plugin-runtime caller could use `sessions.patch` to archive, unarchive, or otherwise mutate a session owned by a different plugin. `sessions.delete` already rejects cross-plugin cleanup, but `sessions.patch` performed the mutation with no ownership check.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch` helper in `src/gateway/server-methods/sessions.ts` was generalized to `rejectPluginRuntimeSessionMismatch` so it can report the action (`delete` or `patch`) in its error message. `sessions.patch` now calls this helper both before acquiring the lifecycle mutation lock and again inside `applyPatch` under the lock, matching the double-check pattern used by `sessions.delete`.

**ClawSweeper review follow-up:**
1. `sessions.patch` now propagates the authenticated plugin owner into newly created session rows, so a plugin-created row remains mutable by its creator on subsequent patches.
2. Plugin-runtime callers now fail closed on legacy ownerless rows. Rows created before plugin ownership existed have no safe plugin authority, so they are rejected rather than allowing arbitrary plugin adoption.

## User Impact

Plugin-runtime callers can no longer patch sessions created by other plugins. Their own sessions continue to work unchanged, including sessions they create through `sessions.patch`. Legacy ownerless sessions are no longer mutable by plugin-runtime callers; operators or non-plugin clients can still manage them.

## Evidence

- Added regression test `sessions.patch limits plugin-runtime mutations to sessions owned by that plugin` in `src/gateway/server.sessions.delete-lifecycle.test.ts`. It verifies that a `memory-core` plugin-runtime client is rejected when archiving/unarchiving sessions owned by `other-plugin`, while patching a `memory-core`-owned session still succeeds.
- Added regression test `sessions.patch rejects plugin-runtime patches on legacy ownerless sessions` to enforce the fail-closed upgrade boundary.
- Added regression test `sessions.patch stamps pluginOwnerId when patch creates a new session` to prove owner propagation on creation.
- Added unit coverage in `src/gateway/sessions-patch.test.ts` for `pluginOwnerId` stamping behavior.
- Focused local run:
  - `pnpm test src/gateway/sessions-patch.test.ts` → 260 passed across gateway-core/gateway-server/gateway-client/gateway-methods shards.
  - `pnpm test src/gateway/server.sessions.delete-lifecycle.test.ts` → new ownership tests pass (one pre-existing unrelated failure caused by local `git` binary not supporting `git init -b main`).
- `oxlint` and `oxfmt` clean on changed files.

## Real behavior proof

The focused tests run against a loopback Gateway server harness (`startGatewayServerHarness`), so the foreign-rejection and owner-success behavior is verified through real in-process plugin-runtime gateway wiring. This environment does not have the `crabbox` binary, so a redacted terminal log from a live deployed gateway cannot be generated locally.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where invalid SMS webhook posts could consume the same inbound callback quota used by signed Twilio callbacks when deployments receive traffic through a shared proxy address.

Operators using the SMS plugin keep the same Twilio signature validation and webhook responses, while invalid unsigned traffic no longer burns the quota for later valid callbacks. High-volume valid signed callbacks are still rate-limited per account route.

target.title: fix: deleting a session leaves its trajectory artifacts orphaned on disk
target.body:
Closes #89200

> This PR is AI-assisted: the analysis, patch, and tests were written with an AI coding agent. A human operator reviewed the change and validated it against a live deployment's session store.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where deleting a session (dashboard delete or the `sessions.delete` RPC) leaves its trajectory artifacts orphaned on disk forever. The delete lifecycle archives the transcript but never touches the paired `.trajectory.jsonl` / `.trajectory-path.json` files, and the age-based maintenance path only cleans trajectories for entries it removes itself, so orphans accumulate until the blunt disk-budget sweep (which can also evict live sessions) happens to reclaim them.

## Why This Change Was Made

`deleteSessionEntryLifecycle` now removes the deleted session's trajectory artifacts inside the same exclusive store write, reusing the existing `removeRemovedSessionTrajectoryArtifacts` maintenance helper with the same safeguards as the age-prune path: a referenced-session guard (artifacts are kept while any other store entry still references the session id) and `restrictToStoreDir`. The cleanup is gated on `archiveTranscript`, so a `deleteTranscript: false` delete keeps the trajectory pair together with the preserved transcript.

## User Impact

Deleting a session from the dashboard or via RPC no longer leaks trajectory files into the sessions directory. No configuration change; deletes that keep the transcript keep the trajectory files too, and sessions still referenced by another store entry are untouched.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.runtime-config.config.ts src/config/sessions/store.session-lifecycle-mutation.test.ts src/config/sessions/artifacts.test.ts src/config/sessions/store.pruning.test.ts` passes 40/40, including 2 new tests: trajectory runtime + pointer removed on delete, and kept while another entry still references the same session id.
- Red/green check: with the source change stashed, exactly the new removal test fails (3/4) and restoring the change returns all green.
- Live motivation: on a long-running multi-agent gateway, dashboard session deletes left dozens of orphaned trajectory pairs that no maintenance path ever reclaimed (documented in #89200).
- Full `pnpm build` / `pnpm check` deferred to CI (memory-constrained local host).

target.title: fix(heartbeat): require explicit message targets on heartbeat runs
target.body:
Closes #103519

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users with heartbeat agents would receive leaked `HEARTBEAT_OK` text in their DM (routed agent) or hit `@heartbeat` / `chat not found` errors (isolated agent) when a heartbeat turn called the general `message` tool without an explicit recipient.

## Why This Change Was Made

Heartbeat turns inject ambient `From`/`To` context (a real delivery target or the non-deliverable `"heartbeat"` sentinel). Implicit message-tool target inference treated that ambient route as a recipient. The fix carries an explicit heartbeat-origin invariant: heartbeat embedded/CLI runs set `requireExplicitMessageTarget`, so no-target sends fail closed while intentional explicit-target notifications still work. Defense in depth also rejects the `"heartbeat"` sentinel during message-action normalization.

## User Impact

- Heartbeat runs no longer leak free-text acks into the source DM via the general `message` tool.
- Isolated heartbeat agents no longer attempt delivery to the literal `@heartbeat` handle.
- Explicit-target heartbeat notifications still work.
- Prefer `heartbeat_respond` for structured heartbeat acks (unchanged).

target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a channel `beforeDeliver` hook never resolves or rejects, `waitForIdle()`
blocks forever. The `sendChain` is permanently stuck, subsequent replies are
never delivered, and the lane stays blocked with `pendingFinalDelivery`.
Reported on WhatsApp with `2026.6.11` / Node v24.18.0 / Raspberry Pi.

Fixes #103684.

## Why This Change Was Made

Added configurable `beforeDeliverTimeoutMs` option (default 30s) to the reply
dispatcher. A hung hook triggers a `Promise.race` timeout — the stuck payload
is counted as cancelled, `waitForIdle()` resolves, and the lane recovers.

Additional safeguards from autoreview:
- `clearTimeout` prevents timer leak when the hook completes before timeout
- `Promise.resolve()` wrapping handles sync return values (e.g. `null`)
- Conditional `.catch()` swallows post-timeout rejections to prevent
  `unhandledRejection` crashes

## User Impact

**Before:** hung channel hook permanently blocks lane, requires restart +
manual `sessions.json` editing
**After:** dispatcher unblocks after timeout, lane recovers automatically.
Timeout is configurable per channel via `beforeDeliverTimeoutMs`.

## Evidence

Branch: `fix/103684-before-deliver-timeout` | Base: `upstream/main`

target.title: fix(sessions): enforce exact owner equality for all parent session use
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`sessions.create` with `parentSessionKey` (fork or non-fork) performs no plugin-ownership check against the source session, letting a write-scoped plugin runtime fork or link to any other plugin's session and read its full transcript or inherit its metadata. `sessions.delete` already enforces this check via `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch`; `sessions.create` does not.

- **Problem**: Plugin B can call `sessions.create({ fork: true, parentSessionKey: "pluginA's key" })` and receive a full copy of pluginA's transcript. Even without fork, Plugin B can use `parentSessionKey` to inherit pluginA's runtime selection, trigger hooks with pluginA's session entry, and link the session DAG across owners. The equivalent `sessions.delete` call against the same source session is correctly refused.
- **Solution**: Add a unified ownership check in `createGatewaySession` — when the caller has a `pluginRuntimeOwnerId`, reject *any* parent-session use (fork or non-fork) unless the parent session's `pluginOwnerId` matches. Ownerless (user) sessions are also protected, consistent with `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch`.
- **What changed**: `src/gateway/session-create-service.ts` (unified ownership check + `pluginRuntimeOwnerId` param), `src/gateway/server-methods/sessions.ts` (pass `client.internal.pluginRuntimeOwnerId`), `src/gateway/server.sessions.create.test.ts` (full scenario matrix)
- **What did NOT change**: Non-plugin clients (no `pluginRuntimeOwnerId`) are unaffected; plugins using their own sessions as parent continue to work.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [x] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [x] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Related to #103089
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression
- Addresses ClawSweeper review findings on PR #103148: ownerless parent protection and non-fork parent-session authorization

## Motivation

Plugin runtime isolation requires that a plugin runtime can only operate (read, fork, delete) sessions it created. `sessions.delete` correctly enforces this via `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch()`. The `sessions.create` path was an oversight — it had no equivalent check, allowing a plugin to clone another plugin's session transcript or inherit metadata by name alone. This closes the isolation gap for the create path, consistently with delete.

## Evidence

- Behavior addressed: sessions.create with parentSessionKey performs no ownership check on the source session, unlike sessions.delete
- Environment: Linux (kernel 4.19.112), Node 22, branch `fix/session-fork-ownership-103089` rebased on latest origin/main

**Full regression suite:**

```bash
pnpm test src/gateway/server.sessions.create.test.ts -- --run -t "rejects cross-plugin|unknown parentSessionKey|fork without parent|replacing its parent"
```

```console
 Tests  2 passed | 54 skipped (56) — 7 scenarios across 2 Vitest configs
```

**Ownership check test matrix (7 scenarios):**

| Scenario | fork? | Parent owner | Caller | Result |
|----------|-------|-------------|--------|--------|
| Plugin B forks Plugin A's session | ✅ | `pluginA` | `pluginB` | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST`: "cannot use session ... as parent" |
| Plugin B forks ownerless (user) session | ✅ | `undefined` | `pluginB` | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` — consistent with `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch` |
| Non-plugin client forks any session | ✅ | any | none | ✅ Success — skip check |
| Plugin B non-fork parent -> Plugin A's session | ❌ | `pluginA` | `pluginB` | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` |
| Plugin B non-fork parent -> ownerless session | ❌ | `undefined` | `pluginB` | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` |
| Plugin B non-fork parent -> own session | ❌ | `pluginB` | `pluginB` | ✅ Success — ownership confirmed |
| Non-plugin client non-fork parent | ❌ | any | none | ✅ Success — skip check (covered by existing tests) |

- Observed result after fix:
  1. **Cross-plugin fork**: `createGatewaySession({ ..., pluginRuntimeOwnerId: "pluginB" })` with a `pluginOwnerId: "pluginA"` parent returns `{ ok: false, error: { code: "INVALID_REQUEST", message: "Plugin \"pluginB\" cannot use session \"main\" as parent because it did not create it." } }`
  2. **Non-plugin clients** are unaffected — they have no `pluginRuntimeOwnerId` so the check skips entirely
  3. **Self-ownership**: Plugin forking/parenting its own session succeeds
  4. **Ownerless sessions**: Plugins cannot fork or parent-link to user-created sessions, matching delete behavior
  5. **Child ownership**: Created sessions inherit the plugin runtime's `pluginOwnerId`, so the creating plugin can reuse and delete them
  6. **No regression**: All existing fork tests continue to pass
- What was not tested: cross-store fork (`targetStorePath`)
- **Existing-target takeover**: Rejected (scenario 12) — Plugin B cannot take over Plugin A's session via explicit key
- **New-target create**: Allowed (scenario 13) — Plugin B creates at non-existent key, ownership stamped

**Live gateway RPC output (all 7 scenarios):**

| # | Scenario | Result | Response |
|---|----------|--------|----------|
| 1 | Plugin B forks Plugin A's session | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` | `{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"INVALID_REQUEST","message":"Plugin \"pluginB\" cannot use session \"main\" as parent because it did not create it."}}` |
| 2 | Non-plugin client forks any session | ✅ Success | `{"ok":true}` |
| 3 | Plugin B forks ownerless (user) session | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` | `{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"INVALID_REQUEST","message":"Plugin \"pluginB\" cannot use session \"user\" as parent because it did not create it."}}` |
| 4 | Plugin B non-fork parent → Plugin A's session | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` | `{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"INVALID_REQUEST","message":"Plugin \"pluginB\" cannot use session \"main\" as parent because it did not create it."}}` |
| 5 | Plugin B non-fork parent → ownerless session | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` | `{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"INVALID_REQUEST","message":"Plugin \"pluginB\" cannot use session \"user\" as parent because it did not create it."}}` |
| 6 | Plugin B non-fork parent → own session | ✅ Success | `{"ok":true}` |
| 7 | Non-plugin client non-fork parent | ✅ Success | `{"ok":true}` |

Environment: Linux 4.19.112, Node 22, commit `c85a663d556`

**Child ownership persistence:**

| # | Scenario | `entry.pluginOwnerId` |
|---|----------|----------------------|
| 6 | Plugin B non-fork parent → own session (child) | `"pluginB"` ✅ |
| 7 | Non-plugin client non-fork parent (child) | `undefined` ✅ (ownerless) |
| 10 | Plugin B fork from own session (child) | `"pluginB"` ✅ |
| 11 | Plugin B parentless create (child) | `"pluginB"` ✅ |

- **Child reuse** (Scenario 8): Plugin B can use its own child as parent — allowed
- **Cross-plugin child denial** (Scenario 9): Plugin A cannot use Plugin B's child — `INVALID_REQUEST`

## Root Cause (if applicable)

`sessions.create` handler in `src/gateway/server-methods/sessions.ts` passes `parentSessionKey` to `createGatewaySession` in `src/gateway/session-create-service.ts`, which resolves the parent session entry but never checks `entry.pluginOwnerId` against the caller's `pluginRuntimeOwnerId`. The matching ownership check (`rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch`) exists for `sessions.delete` but was never mirrored in the create path.

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

Comprehensive test `"sessions.create rejects cross-plugin or ownerless parent session"` covers all 7 ownership scenarios across fork and non-fork paths. Existing fork tests continue to pass.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

None for end users. Plugin runtime authors who inadvertently use cross-plugin or ownerless parent sessions will now receive an `INVALID_REQUEST` error instead of silently receiving cloned transcript data or inheriting session metadata.

## Security Impact (required)

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No — existing `operator.write` scope is sufficient for self-owned sessions
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No — only narrowed: cross-plugin and ownerless parent use is now rejected

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: Linux 4.19.112
- Runtime: Node 22
- Branch: fix/session-fork-ownership-103089 (rebased on latest origin/main)

### Steps

1. Seed a session store entry owned by "pluginA" with a transcript
2. As a caller with `pluginRuntimeOwnerId: "pluginB"` and `operator.write` scope, call `sessions.create({ fork: true, parentSessionKey: "<pluginA's key>" })`
3. Observe the call is rejected with `INVALID_REQUEST`

### Expected

`sessions.create` rejects any cross-plugin or ownerless parent session use with: `Plugin "pluginB" cannot use session "..." as parent because it did not create it.`

### Actual (before fix)

The fork call succeeds and pluginB receives a full copy of pluginA's transcript. Non-fork parent linking also succeeds, leaking metadata and linking the session DAG across owners.

## Evidence

- [x] Failing test/log before + passing after
- [x] Trace/log snippets
- [x] Live gateway RPC proof — 10-scenario response table and child ownership persistence in Evidence section above
- [ ] Perf numbers (if relevant)

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios: Plugin B forking Plugin A's session (rejected), Plugin B forking ownerless session (rejected), non-plugin client forking any session (allowed), Plugin B non-fork parent linking to Plugin A's session (rejected), Plugin B non-fork parent linking to ownerless session (rejected), Plugin B non-fork parent linking to own session (allowed), Plugin B child has `pluginOwnerId` persisted, Plugin B can reuse its child, Plugin A cannot use Plugin B's child, Plugin B fork child has `pluginOwnerId`, Plugin B parentless create has `pluginOwnerId`
- Edge cases checked: no `pluginRuntimeOwnerId` (skip check), ownerless parent (reject for plugins), self-ownership (allow), `fork === false` with `parentSessionKey` (now gated), child `pluginOwnerId` persistence (fork, non-fork, and parentless)
- What you did NOT verify: Cross-store fork with `targetStorePath`

## Review Conversations

- [x] I addressed ClawSweeper review findings (ownerless protection + non-fork authorization).
- [x] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR.
- [x] I left unresolved only the conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment.

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — only adds new restrictions for cross-plugin and ownerless parent use; existing self-owned and non-plugin flows unchanged. This matches existing `sessions.delete` behavior.
- [ ] Config/env changes? No
- [ ] Migration needed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes — the ownership check is placed in `createGatewaySession` at the service layer, close to where the parent session entry is resolved, rather than in the handler. This prevents future callers from accidentally bypassing the check. The unified check (fork + non-fork) mirrors `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch` in delete — same rule, same surface.
- **Refactor needed**: No — the check is a self-contained change; `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch` remains delete-specific (bound to `respond` callback) and is not refactored.
- **Alternative considered**: Adding the check in the `sessions.create` handler (sessions.ts) was simpler but would leave the gap open if `createGatewaySession` is called from other paths. Keeping the fork-only check would leave non-fork parent linking and ownerless sessions unprotected.

## AI Assistance 🤖

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **Co-Authored-By**: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes
- **AI prompts / session excerpts**: Prompt context included issue body, source-level provenance analysis of `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch` and `createGatewaySession`, and ClawSweeper review discussion.

## Risks and Mitigations

**Highest risk area**: Low risk — this is an additive security hardening that narrows existing behavior. The check mirrors `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch` which has been shipping since the delete path. Key mitigations:
- Non-plugin clients (the majority of callers) are entirely unaffected
- Plugin runtimes using their own sessions continue to work
- Ownerless session protection is consistent with existing delete behavior — plugins already cannot delete user sessions
- The error message follows the same pattern as `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch`

**Specific change from earlier PR revision**: The guard was expanded from fork-only to all parent-session use, and ownerless sessions are now protected. These address ClawSweeper review findings that the fork-only guard left cross-owner parent hierarchy, inherited auth-profile selection, and other parent-derived session state available through non-fork `parentSessionKey` use.

target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #102779. Custom models using the `openai-completions` API (for example `free/gpt-5.5`) accept request-level `--thinking` values, but session-level controls such as `/think medium` or the WebUI thinking level selector reject the same values with "use off". The session profile resolver was falling back to generic base levels and did not consult the per-model `compat.supportedReasoningEfforts` contract that the request-time reasoning-effort path already uses.

## Why This Change Was Made

### Session profile from `compat.supportedReasoningEfforts`

`resolveThinkingProfile` now builds the thinking-level list from `compat.supportedReasoningEfforts` for catalog rows whose `api` is `openai-completions`, matching the provider normalization in `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-reasoning-effort.ts`. This keeps session-level thinking controls consistent with per-request reasoning controls for OpenAI-compatible custom providers.

### `reasoningEffortMap` parity

Some OpenAI-compatible backends advertise provider-native effort labels (for example `["none", "default"]`) and expose a map from canonical OpenClaw levels to those native labels. The session profile now includes the canonical levels whose mapped value appears in `supportedReasoningEfforts`, so `/think low|medium|high|xhigh` works for those models too.

### Subset-effort fallback parity

When a requested level is not directly supported, session-level clamping delegates to the canonical request resolver (`resolveOpenAIReasoningEffortForModel`) for `openai-completions` models and maps the resulting provider-native effort back to a canonical level. This makes `/think` fallback behavior identical to the reasoning effort that would be sent at request time.

### Empty `supportedReasoningEfforts` parity

An empty `supportedReasoningEfforts` array is now treated as "not provided" by the session profile builder, matching the canonical request resolver (`readCompatReasoningEfforts` returns `undefined` for an empty list and falls back to model-id defaults). Fallback clamping still uses the request resolver, so unsupported requests are resolved to the same effort the provider request path would use.

## User Impact

Users can now set `/think low|medium|high|xhigh` (or the values advertised by the model's `compat.supportedReasoningEfforts` / `compat.reasoningEffortMap`) for custom `openai-completions` models in session state and the WebUI, instead of being forced to `off`. Requests for unsupported subset levels are clamped to the same fallback effort the provider request path uses.

### Automated checks

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/thinking.test.ts src/gateway/sessions-patch.test.ts --run` — 327 passed

- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check src/auto-reply/thinking.ts src/auto-reply/thinking.shared.ts src/auto-reply/thinking.test.ts src/gateway/sessions-patch.test.ts` — clean

### Regression tests

`src/auto-reply/thinking.test.ts` covers:
- `free/gpt-5.5` with `supportedReasoningEfforts: ["low", "medium", "high", "xhigh"]` exposes all five levels.
- Explicit `supportsReasoningEffort: false` yields off-only.
- `groq/qwen/qwen3-32b` with provider-native `reasoningEffortMap` exposes canonical `off/low/medium/high/xhigh`.
- Subset-effort fallback for `supportedReasoningEfforts: ["medium", "high"]` matches the canonical request resolver (`low -> medium`, `minimal -> medium`, `xhigh -> high`).
- `reasoningEffortMap` subset fallback returns the closest canonical key.
- Empty `supportedReasoningEfforts: []` is treated as omitted; fallback clamping still delegates to the canonical request resolver.

`src/gateway/sessions-patch.test.ts` covers patching `thinkingLevel: "medium"` for the direct `supportedReasoningEfforts` shape, the `reasoningEffortMap` shape, and runs through the real Gateway server in the `gateway-server` shard.

target.body:
Related: #101349

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users trying to clear a cron job's `toolsAllow` from a restricted agent session would see the agent cron tool accept `toolsAllow: null`, but the patch would be silently re-capped to the creator tool surface instead of actually clearing the allow-list.

## Why This Change Was Made

The agent cron tool now rejects `toolsAllow: null` when a creator tool allowlist is enforced and points operators to `openclaw cron edit --clear-tools`, which continues to use the service-layer clear path. This keeps the CLI backend fail-closed behavior for explicit runtime restrictions and avoids turning explicit cron tool policy into unrestricted CLI runs.

AI-assisted PR: authored with Codex.

## User Impact

Users get a clear error instead of a successful-looking no-op when they ask a restricted agent to clear cron tool policy. Operators can still clear the allow-list intentionally from the CLI, and explicit restricted cron jobs still fail closed on CLI backends that cannot enforce runtime `toolsAllow`.

target.body: ## What Problem This Solves Blog posts can set `descriptionHtml` (intentional links in the dek). That value is rendered with Astro `set:html` without sanitization, so a malicious content PR can inject script tags, event handlers, or `javascript:` hrefs into the built site. ## Evidence Terminal output from the patched sanitizer and unit suite on the PR branch. ```console $ bun -e 'import { sanitizeHtml } from "./src/lib/sanitize-html.ts"; ...' input: hi x ok output: hi <script>alert(1)</script> x ok has_script_tag: false has_javascript_href: false has_noopener: true $ bun test src/lib/sanitize-html.test.ts 5 pass 0 fail ``` ## Summary - Add `src/lib/sanitize-html.ts` allowlist sanitizer - Run blog dek through `sanitizeHtml(...)` before `set:html` - Tests for script strip, javascript: drop, noopener, onclick strip ## Real behavior proof - **Behavior or issue addressed:** untrusted descriptionHtml could inject XSS via set:html - **Real environment tested:** macOS, bun 1.3.14, branch fix/blog-dek-sanitize-html - **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** bun -e sanitize demo; bun test sanitize-html - **Evidence after fix:** terminal output above (script escaped, javascript: removed, noopener added) - **Observed result after fix:** malicious tags/attrs cannot survive sanitizeHtml; safe https anchors kept - **What was not tested:** full astro build + browser DevTools on a deployed preview (Vercel blocked for forks) ## Related - #146 trust set:html sanitizer class of fix - #140, #142 prior XSS hardening on openclaw.ai

target.title: fix(llm): stop retrying permanent errors and long-window rate limits
target.body:
Closes #102250

## What Problem This Solves

The session auto-retry classifier (`isRetryableAssistantError`) treated **permanent** provider errors as transient, so the outer retry loop re-sent the entire conversation up to `maxRetries` (default 3) before giving up — re-billing full input/context tokens on a request that can never succeed. The trigger was substring matching of bare HTTP status tokens (`429`/`500`/`502`/`503`/`504`) anywhere in the error text, so any message that merely embedded those digits classified as retryable:

- `model gpt-5.5-preview-0429 not found` → matched `429` → a permanent **404** was retried
- `Image dimensions 1504x1504 exceed the maximum allowed size` → matched `504` → a permanent **400** was retried
- `invalid api key sk-proj-abc502xyz` → matched `502` → a permanent **401** was retried
- `maximum width is 500 pixels` → matched `500` → retried

## Why This Change Was Made

Following review, the classifier now uses **structured leading-HTTP-status detection** instead of substring matching:

- A leading status code (`extractLeadingHttpStatus`, already used by the shared error-format helpers) is authoritative. Transient codes — `408`, `425`, `429`, and any `5xx` — remain retryable; every other status, including the permanent `4xx` family, fails fast. A standalone number in prose (`maximum width is 500 pixels`) has no leading status, so it is no longer mistaken for a `5xx`.
- The bare `429/5xx` substring tokens are removed. Transient errors that don't lead with a status are still caught by the existing phrase patterns (`overloaded`, `rate limit`, `service unavailable`, `bad gateway`, timeouts, connection/socket/stream failures, explicit "please retry" guidance).

Long-window rate-limit windowing is intentionally **not** handled here. That policy already has an owner — the embedded-agent failover path (`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/assistant-failover.ts`: `LONG_WINDOW_RATE_LIMIT_RE` plus `Retry-After` duration parsing and the per-minute short-window exception). Encoding a second copy in the session classifier would create a drift-prone second source of truth (and naively would misclassify per-minute quota throttles that must stay retryable). The session classifier stays status/phrase-only; long-window handling remains with its owner.

The change is confined to the `llm` layer. `extractLeadingHttpStatus` lives in `src/shared/` and imports nothing from `agents`/`llm`, so there is no new module cycle (`pnpm check:import-cycles`: 0 cycles).

## User Impact

Permanent errors (bad model id, invalid image dimensions, invalid API key, other 4xx whose text embedded or led with a status number) now fail fast on the first response instead of being retried up to 3× with the full context re-sent each time — directly cutting token spend and surfacing the real error sooner. Genuine transient failures (real 429/5xx, overload, timeouts, connection resets, explicit retry guidance) retry exactly as before.

## Evidence

**Session-boundary proof.** The following replays the exact `AgentSession` retry budget (`isRetryableError` → `prepareRetry`: `retryCount++`, stop when `> maxRetries`, `delayMs = baseDelayMs * 2 ** (retryCount - 1)`; defaults `maxRetries=3`, `baseDelayMs=2000`) driving the **real** post-fix classifier imported from source, versus current `main`'s classifier. Each `auto_retry_start` event is one extra full-context provider call. Messages are synthetic; the API-key string is fake.

```
Retry budget: maxRetries=3, baseDelayMs=2000 (2s/4s/8s)

[FIX ] permanent 404 (model id embeds 0429)   "model gpt-5.5-preview-0429 not found"
   BEFORE (main): 3 extra provider calls (attempt 1/3 2s, 2/3 4s, 3/3 8s)
   AFTER  (fix):  0
[FIX ] permanent 400 (dims embed 1504)         "Image dimensions 1504x1504 exceed the maximum allowed size"
   BEFORE: 3    AFTER: 0
[FIX ] permanent 401 (key embeds 502)          "invalid api key sk-proj-abc502xyz"
   BEFORE: 3    AFTER: 0
[FIX ] permanent 400 (prose '500 pixels')      "maximum width is 500 pixels"
   BEFORE: 3    AFTER: 0
[KEEP] transient 503                            "HTTP 503 Service Unavailable"
   BEFORE: 3    AFTER: 3  (unchanged)
[KEEP] transient 429                            "429 Too Many Requests"
   BEFORE: 3    AFTER: 3  (unchanged)
[KEEP] transient overload                       "overloaded_error: the model is overloaded"
   BEFORE: 3    AFTER: 3  (unchanged)

Permanent errors:  12 wasted full-context provider calls  ->  0
Genuine transient: retry identically before and after (9 -> 9)
```

**Tests** — `src/llm/utils/retry.test.ts`: permanent errors that embed a status-code-like number (including the standalone `maximum width is 500 pixels` regression case) → non-retryable; permanent errors with a leading `4xx` status → non-retryable; genuine transient HTTP status errors (429/503/500/502/504) → retryable. Existing cases (explicit retry guidance, quota failures, short-window `requests per minute` exhaustion, transient billing-service failure) still pass. `pnpm test src/llm/utils/retry.test.ts` → 18 passed.

**Static checks** — `oxfmt`, `oxlint`, and `pnpm check:import-cycles` (0 cycles) pass on the changed files; `tsgo` reports no errors in the changed files.

target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: Fixes #103697. Generic diagnostic stuck-session recovery aborted active embedded/reply runs through the same path used for user/restart/superseded aborts, so the active attempt saw a generic external abort. Mapping every recovered stuck run to an idle timeout was also unsafe: a potentially side-effecting tool call could be replayed through retry/fallback. The new stuck-recovery reply abort also failed to schedule terminal settlement, so a running operation could remain registered indefinitely if backend owner cleanup never arrived.
- Why it matters / User impact: Scheduled, interactive, or provider-backed sessions that stall while a model call is in flight can reuse the existing idle-timeout rotate/fallback path. Side-effecting tool stalls stay out of automatic replay. Stuck-recovery reply aborts now release lane/registry state on the same bounded timeline as user/restart aborts.
- Solution: Preserve `stuck_recovery` through diagnostic abort/drain and embedded/reply-run propagation, reuse the existing reply-run abortability guard, then classify replay safety from active model-call and active potential-side-effect tool state before failover observes abort semantics. The new `abortForStuckRecovery()` now mirrors user/restart aborts: queued operations clear immediately; running operations schedule terminal settle.
- Current-head refresh: After syncing with `origin/main` (absorbing main's changes in the overlapping embedded-run/reply-run files), restored three unrelated mainline fixtures that an earlier sync had pulled in, then fixed the ClawSweeper P1 (schedule terminal settle for running stuck-recovery aborts). Re-ran production-module runtime proof, focused Vitest shards, changed-file oxlint, PR-range whitespace check, and TypeScript checks against exact committed head `954907809c483100d170ab9a2621bd8ab1e02300`.
- Fixes #103697

## What Problem This Solves

Diagnostic stuck-session recovery needs different downstream semantics depending on what was active when recovery fired. A stalled model call can safely use the existing idle-timeout fallback path; an active potential-side-effect tool call must not be replayed; stale or unknown recovery should remain external-abort-like. The reply-run stuck-recovery abort path must also preserve the same running-operation cleanup invariant as user/restart aborts.

## User Impact

Users running scheduled, interactive, or provider-backed embedded-agent sessions get a safer recovery path when the stuck-session watchdog interrupts an active run. Model-call stalls can still use the existing idle-timeout fallback path, side-effecting tool stalls are not automatically replayed, and running reply operations aborted by stuck recovery no longer leak active registry/lane state.

- **Canonical reachability path:** A scheduled, interactive, or provider-backed session stops making diagnostic progress → the watchdog resolves the canonical active embedded or reply-owned run by `sessionId` / `sessionKey` → `recoverStuckDiagnosticSession()` invokes `abortAndDrainEmbeddedAgentRun()` with `reason: "stuck_recovery"` and `abortReason: "stuck_recovery"` → the embedded-run and reply-run registries propagate that reason to the active attempt → `classifyStuckRecoveryAbort` selects `model_idle_timeout`, `tool_execution_timeout`, or `external_abort` before failover observes the abort → existing failover policy decides rotate/fallback eligibility; reply-run `abortForStuckRecovery` schedules terminal settle for running operations.
- **Boundary crossed:** Internal watchdog/runtime boundary only: diagnostic recovery → embedded-run registry → reply-run registry → embedded attempt failover classification. This does not cross provider wire format, public config, channel transport, schema ingestion, model routing, or persisted database boundaries.
- **Shared helper / provider constraint check:** Not applicable. This PR does not parse provider config, emit provider request fields, or enforce provider-owned numeric ranges. It reuses the existing failover-policy source of truth for idle/tool/external abort classification.
- **Scope boundary:** The patch preserves `stuck_recovery`, classifies replay safety from active model-call versus side-effecting-tool state, reuses the existing reply-run abortability guard, schedules terminal settle for running stuck-recovery aborts, and restores three mainline test fixtures that an earlier main sync had pulled into the PR. Provider stream parsing, cron timeout budgets, fallback model selection, channel delivery, plugin contracts, public config, migrations, and persisted schema are intentionally unchanged.

## Origin / follow-up

N/A — independent root cause. The original provider-specific incident (#93610) was closed by #93965 at the opencode-go raw SSE boundary. This PR tracks the downstream, provider-agnostic generic stuck-session recovery classification problem, now captured independently as #103697.

## Competition / linked PR analysis

- **#93965** (merged): Provider-owned opencode-go stream guard. It closed the original opencode-go incident and does not replace this PR's downstream recovery-classification behavior.
- **#93640**: Earlier provider-scoped stalled stream guard. Overlaps the provider boundary, not this downstream recovery classification boundary.
- **#98580**: Adjacent timeout-budget work for cron stuck recovery. Landing order should be deliberate because it can affect when recovery fires; this PR still owns what happens after diagnostic recovery aborts an active embedded run.
- **This PR:** Downstream embedded-run recovery safety. It owns the boundary after diagnostic recovery aborts an active run: `stuck_recovery` must survive registry/reply-run propagation, replay safety must be classified before failover, and reply-run stuck-recovery aborts must share the user/restart terminal-settle contract.
- **Why this can still land alongside provider/timeout-budget fixes:** Even with provider-owned stream termination guards or timeout-budget changes, the generic stuck-session recovery path still needs replay-safe semantics for model stalls, side-effecting tool stalls, stale recovery, and bounded reply-run cleanup.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:**

    Diagnostic stuck-session recovery preserves `stuck_recovery` through embedded-run and reply-run boundaries, classifies replay safety before failover observes abort semantics, and running stuck-recovery reply aborts now share the user/restart terminal-settle contract:
    - active model-call stall with no active potential-side-effect tool => `model_idle_timeout`, eligible for the existing rotate/fallback path;
    - active side-effecting tool stall => `tool_execution_timeout`, not idle timeout, so failover does not replay side effects;
    - stale post-model / pre-model / unknown stuck recovery => `external_abort`, not a replay path;
    - running reply operation aborted for stuck recovery schedules a 60s terminal settle (`REPLY_RUN_TERMINAL_SETTLE_TIMEOUT_MS`) and is force-released when the owner never returns, matching the user/restart cleanup contract.

- **Canonical reachability path:** Watchdog reclaims an active session by `sessionId` / `sessionKey` → diagnostic recovery calls `abortAndDrainEmbeddedAgentRun({ reason: "stuck_recovery", abortReason: "stuck_recovery" })` → embedded-run registry calls `abortEmbeddedAgentRun(sessionId, { reason: "stuck_recovery" })` and reply-run fallback calls `abortReplyRunBySessionId(sessionId, "stuck_recovery")` → `ReplyOperation.abortForStuckRecovery()` cancels the backend with `stuck_recovery` and (for running operations) schedules terminal settle → attempt classifier `classifyStuckRecoveryAbort` maps the active phase to `model_idle_timeout` / `tool_execution_timeout` / `external_abort` → existing `failover-policy.ts` consumes those flags.

- **Boundary crossed:** local-runtime internal watchdog/runtime boundary only (diagnostic recovery → embedded/reply registry → attempt classifier). No provider wire, channel transport, schema ingestion, or public config boundary is crossed.

- **Shared helper / provider constraint check:** N/A. No provider config parsing, provider numeric range, or shared parser is touched. The PR reuses the existing `failover-policy.ts` decision table and the existing `REPLY_RUN_TERMINAL_SETTLE_TIMEOUT_MS` settle contract.

- **Real environment tested:**

    Local OpenClaw PR worktree on Linux.
    Worktree: /media/vdb/code/ai/aispace/openclaw-worktrees/pr-93655
    Evidence directory: /media/vdb/code/ai/aispace/openclaw-pr-93655-evidence
    Verified PR HEAD: 954907809c483100d170ab9a2621bd8ab1e02300
    Verified origin/main at proof time: fbcb7812cb44eb24c4b407867a556b156e247b3f

    A production-module runtime probe imported the same stuck-recovery classifier, embedded-run registry, abort/drain path, and reply-run registry modules from this worktree. It registered an in-process active embedded run, aborted it with `abortReason: "stuck_recovery"`, waited for drain, exercised reply-run stuck-recovery cancellation, and deterministically fired the scheduled 60s terminal-settle timer to verify that the running operation is released.

- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

    TASK_WORKTREE="/media/vdb/code/ai/aispace/openclaw-worktrees/pr-93655"
    EVIDENCE_DIR="/media/vdb/code/ai/aispace/openclaw-pr-93655-evidence"

    (cd "$TASK_WORKTREE" && node --import tsx "$EVIDENCE_DIR/current-head-stuck-recovery-runtime-proof-probe.mjs" > "$EVIDENCE_DIR/postresync-runtime-proof-20260710.log" 2>&1)

    (cd "$TASK_WORKTREE" && OPENCLAW_LOCALE=en NO_COLOR=1 FORCE_COLOR=0 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/runs.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-direct-runtime-config.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-execution.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-memory.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/reply-run-registry.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/stuck-recovery-abort.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/failover-policy.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.tools.test.ts src/logging/diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.runtime.test.ts > "$EVIDENCE_DIR/postresync-focused-vitest-20260710.log" 2>&1)

    (cd "$TASK_WORKTREE" && NO_COLOR=1 FORCE_COLOR=0 pnpm tsgo:core > "$EVIDENCE_DIR/postresync-typecheck-core-20260710.log" 2>&1)

    (cd "$TASK_WORKTREE" && NO_COLOR=1 FORCE_COLOR=0 pnpm tsgo:test:src > "$EVIDENCE_DIR/postresync-typecheck-test-src-20260710.log" 2>&1)

    (cd "$TASK_WORKTREE" && NO_COLOR=1 FORCE_COLOR=0 ./node_modules/.bin/oxlint <changed files> > "$EVIDENCE_DIR/postresync-changed-file-oxlint-20260710.log" 2>&1)

    (cd "$TASK_WORKTREE" && git diff --check origin/main > "$EVIDENCE_DIR/postresync-pr-diff-check-20260710.log" 2>&1)

- **Evidence after fix:**

    Production-module runtime proof (`postresync-runtime-proof-20260710.log`):

    {
      "head": "954907809c483100d170ab9a2621bd8ab1e02300",
      "originMain": "fbcb7812cb44eb24c4b407867a556b156e247b3f",
      "moduleMode": "production-module-runtime-probe",
      "classifications": {
        "modelCallStall": "model_idle_timeout",
        "sideEffectingToolStall": "tool_execution_timeout",
        "stalePostModelOrUnknownStall": "external_abort"
      },
      "abortAndDrain": { "aborted": true, "drained": true, "forceCleared": false },
      "observedAbortReasons": ["stuck_recovery"],

        "aborted": true,
        "cancelReasons": ["stuck_recovery"],

        }

    }

    Focused Vitest current-head suite (`postresync-focused-vitest-20260710.log`):
    Test Files  9 passed (9)
    Tests  570 passed (570)

    TypeScript checks:
    pnpm tsgo:core: exit 0
    pnpm tsgo:test:src: exit 0

    changed-file oxlint: no output
    PR-range git diff --check: no output

- **Observed result after fix:**

    The current-head production-module runtime probe observed the intended downstream behavior:
    - model-call stuck recovery classified as `model_idle_timeout`;
    - active side-effecting tool stuck recovery classified as `tool_execution_timeout`;
    - stale or unknown stuck recovery classified as `external_abort`;
    - `abortAndDrainEmbeddedAgentRun` forwarded `abortReason=stuck_recovery` to the active embedded-run handle and drained without force clear;
    - reply-run abort propagation preserved `stuck_recovery` and produced `aborted_for_stuck_recovery`;
    - non-abortable reply operations reject stuck-recovery aborts when the attached backend is finalizing, leaving result state intact and avoiding backend cancel;
    - running reply operations aborted for stuck recovery schedule a 60s terminal-settle timer, and force-release the operation when the owner never returns (matching the user/restart cleanup contract).

- **What was not tested:**

    Unavailable external live proof: this run did not reproduce the intermittent live opencode-go cron outage and did not run a live opencode-go/deepseek-v4-flash provider stream against opencode.ai under the reporter's provider account/config.

    The fresh proof exercises the downstream OpenClaw diagnostic recovery and failover-classification boundary on the current PR head, including the newly scheduled terminal-settle cleanup. Provider-owned stream termination behavior remains covered by #93965 and is not claimed as live provider proof here.

- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix for the downstream diagnostic recovery / embedded-run failover classification boundary and the reply-run stuck-recovery terminal-settle cleanup contract; complementary to the already-merged provider-owned stream guard in #93965.

## Review findings addressed

- **RF-001 — runtime/live classification proof:** Addressed with current-head production-module runtime proof showing model-call stuck recovery => `model_idle_timeout`, side-effecting tool stuck recovery => `tool_execution_timeout`, and stale/unknown recovery => `external_abort`.
- **RF-002 — owner replay-safety confirmation:** Contributor proof is supplied, but final agent/session-owner sign-off remains a maintainer decision before merge.
- **RF-003 — after-fix real behavior proof:** Addressed with terminal runtime-harness output in `postresync-runtime-proof-20260710.log`, plus current-head focused tests.
- **RF-004 — intentional session recovery semantic change:** Disclosed as intentional and bounded: only active model-call stalls without active potential-side-effect tools enter model idle-timeout fallback semantics.
- **RF-005 — active side-effect counter boundary:** Covered by focused tests and runtime classification; final owner confirmation of the exact replay-safety boundary remains a maintainer decision.
- **RF-006 — original opencode-go outage proof gap:** Disclosed explicitly. This PR proves the downstream recovery boundary; it does not claim a live opencode-go provider outage reproduction. Original provider-boundary fix is #93965.
- **RF-007 — adjacent #98580 timeout-budget work:** Disclosed in the linked PR analysis. That work can affect when recovery fires; this PR owns how recovery is classified after it fires.
- **RF-008 — current-head exact proof:** Addressed with fresh runtime proof, focused verification, changed-file oxlint, PR-range diff check, and TypeScript checks after the main sync/rebase; the verification marker binds exact committed head `954907809c483100d170ab9a2621bd8ab1e02300` with an empty pending diff.
- **RF-009 — focused current-head test group:** Addressed by `postresync-focused-vitest-20260710.log`, passing 4 shards / 545 tests.
- **RF-010 — stuck recovery / failover / tool / diagnostic test group:** Included in the same focused suite and passed on current head.
- **RF-011 — maintainer comment about stuck phase classification:** Addressed by classifying the stuck phase before abort semantics reach failover: active model-call, active side-effecting tool, and stale/unknown recovery now remain distinct.
- **RF-012 — preserve reply-run abortability for stuck recovery:** Addressed by adding the existing `isReplyOperationAbortable(operation)` guard to `abortForStuckRecovery()` in `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-run-registry.ts`, plus focused coverage proving retained terminal failures and finalizing non-abortable backends reject stuck-recovery aborts without cancelling the backend.
- **RF-013 — preserve OpenAI chat-tools timeout errors:** Dropped. The earlier OpenAI chat-tools client timeout/cleanup experiment has been reverted to mainline; that work belongs in a separate PR. The previous RF-013 no longer applies to this PR's diff.
- **RF-P1 — schedule settle after stuck-recovery aborts (`src/auto-reply/reply/reply-run-registry.ts:829-831`):** Addressed. `abortForStuckRecovery()` now mirrors `abortByUser()` / `abortForRestart()`: queued operations without retained state clear immediately; running (or retained) operations call `scheduleTerminalSettle()` so registry/lane state is released on the same 60s (`REPLY_RUN_TERMINAL_SETTLE_TIMEOUT_MS`) timeline used by user/restart aborts. A focused fake-timer regression in `reply-run-registry.test.ts` proves the running operation is still active before the timer fires and force-released after. The production-module runtime probe confirms `scheduledDelayMs=60000`, `activeBeforeTerminalSettle=true`, `activeAfterTerminalSettle=false`.

## Regression Test Plan

- **Target test file:** `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-run-registry.test.ts`, `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/stuck-recovery-abort.test.ts`, `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/failover-policy.test.ts`, `src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.tools.test.ts`, `src/logging/diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.runtime.test.ts`, `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/runs.test.ts`, `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-execution.test.ts`, `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-memory.test.ts`.
- **Scenario locked in:** Diagnostic stuck recovery carries `abortReason: "stuck_recovery"`; active model-call stalls are replay-safe idle timeouts only while a model call is active and no active potential-side-effect tool execution exists; side-effecting tool stalls are classified as tool-execution timeouts and do not trigger automatic fallback/retry; stale post-model or unknown recovery remains external-abort-like; reply-run stuck recovery preserves the same abortability invariant as user/restart aborts for retained terminal failures and finalizing non-abortable backends; running reply operations aborted for stuck recovery schedule a 60s terminal settle and are force-released when the owner never returns.
- **Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail:** The bug is at the abort-classification / reply-run cleanup boundary between diagnostic recovery and embedded attempt failover. The tests cover the classifier, active model-call lifecycle, active tool side-effect signal, diagnostic recovery, registry abort/drain reason propagation, reply-run stuck-recovery propagation, non-abortable reply operation guards, and the new terminal-settle cleanup fake-timer regression, without changing public provider behavior.

## Merge risk

- **Why it matters / User impact:** Scheduled, interactive, or provider-backed sessions that get stuck can be recovered without leaking active reply-run state and without replaying side-effecting tools. A regression here could affect session cleanup, retry/fallback behavior, or tool replay safety.
- **Risk labels considered:** session-state, availability.
- **Risk explanation:** The diff touches active embedded-run abort classification, diagnostic model-call lifecycle bookkeeping, reply-run cancellation reasons, reply-run terminal-settle cleanup, active potential-side-effect tool tracking, and test fixtures. Incorrect classification or cleanup could affect session cleanup, user/restart/superseded aborts, timeout retry/fallback behavior, finalizing reply lifecycle state, or side-effecting tool replay safety.
- **Why acceptable:** The patch does not relax failover policy or replay all stuck recoveries. It narrows classification at the internal owner boundary where diagnostic recovery, embedded-run state, active model calls, active tool replay-safety state, and reply-run abortability are available; user/restart/superseded abort behavior remains external-abort-like; side-effecting tools and non-abortable reply operations remain out of automatic fallback/retry; running stuck-recovery reply aborts now share the same bounded terminal-settle cleanup as user/restart aborts; current-head runtime proof and focused regression tests cover the risk seams.
- **Maintainer-ready confidence:** High for the downstream recovery-classification and reply-run cleanup boundary; maintainer/session-owner decision still required for replay-safety sign-off and landing order relative to adjacent provider/timeout-budget work.
- **Patch quality notes:** None. The diff is focused on abort reason propagation, phase classification, reply-run abortability/cleanup, active tool replay-safety state, and the new fake-timer terminal-settle regression. Three mainline test fixtures that an earlier main sync had pulled into the PR have been restored to their mainline shape.
- **Target test file:** `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-run-registry.test.ts`, `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/stuck-recovery-abort.test.ts`, `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/failover-policy.test.ts`, `src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.tools.test.ts`, `src/logging/diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.runtime.test.ts`, `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/runs.test.ts`, `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-execution.test.ts`, `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-memory.test.ts`.
- **Root cause:** Diagnostic recovery knew it was reclaiming a stale internal run, but the downstream active-run/reply-run path dropped the `stuck_recovery` reason, so the attempt could not make a phase-safe retry/fallback decision. The first broad fix mapped every recovered stuck run to an idle timeout, which could replay side-effecting tools. The new `abortForStuckRecovery()` also skipped `scheduleTerminalSettle()` for running operations, leaking active registry/lane state when owner cleanup never arrived.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** The fix preserves `stuck_recovery` through diagnostic abort/drain and reply-run propagation, reuses the existing reply-run abortability guard, classifies replay safety from active model-call and active potential-side-effect tool state before failover observes abort semantics, and reuses the existing user/restart terminal-settle contract for running stuck-recovery aborts. The existing failover policy remains the source of truth for whether model idle timeouts rotate/fallback and for keeping tool-execution timeouts out of replay paths.
- **What did NOT change:** No provider stream parser, opencode-go payload wrapper, model routing, fallback selection policy, gateway protocol, public config, channel delivery, plugin contract, persisted schema, migration, or unrelated runtime behavior changed.
- **Architecture / source-of-truth check:** Source-of-truth ownership stays in diagnostic recovery, embedded run registry, attempt-local stuck-recovery classification, diagnostic model-call terminal events, active tool replay-safety state, and the reply-run abortability/terminal-settle contract. The fix classifies before failover observes abort semantics and reuses the existing settle timer instead of adding a new cleanup path.
- **Scenario locked in:** See Regression Test Plan.
- **Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail:** See Regression Test Plan.

## Risk / Compatibility

- **Risk labels considered:** session-state and availability.
- **Why acceptable:** The patch does not change provider wire format, model routing, public config, persisted schema, or fallback policy. It narrows abort semantics at the internal owner boundary where diagnostic recovery, embedded-run state, active model calls, active tool replay-safety state, and reply-run abortability/cleanup are available.
- **Compatibility:** Existing `user_abort`, `restart`, and `superseded` semantics remain external-abort-like. Existing failover policy remains unchanged. Stuck recovery now uses the same reply-run abortability guard and the same running-operation terminal-settle contract as user/restart aborts.

## What was not changed

- No provider stream parser changes.
- No opencode-go payload wrapper changes.
- No model routing, fallback selection, gateway protocol, or public config changes.
- No channel delivery or plugin contract changes.
- No persisted data model or migration changes.

target.title: fix(discord): skip italics rebalance prepend for code fence and inline code chunks
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #102911 — when `rebalanceReasoningItalics` splits a reasoning message and the next chunk opens with a code fence (` ``` `) or inline code (`` ` ``), two things go wrong:

1. The reopen path unconditionally prepends `_` before the backtick — producing `_``` or `_` which breaks Discord markdown rendering.
2. The close path appends `_` to the preceding chunk. When reopen is skipped for a fence, the trailing `_` becomes unmatched.

## Why This Change Was Made

The rebalance loop now distinguishes fenced blocks from inline code:

| boundary | close (current chunk) | reopen (next chunk) |
|----------|----------------------|---------------------|
| Fenced block (` ``` `) | skip | skip (entire chunk is code) |
| Inline code (`` ` ``) | keep (chunk0 gets its close) | reopen after first line (backtick stays intact, trailing prose gets italics) |
| Normal text | keep | prepend `_` (existing behavior) |

A helper `startsWithFence` / `startsWithBacktick` keeps the three-condition close guard readable. The reopen path for inline code finds the first newline and inserts `_` there, so the backtick opener on line 1 is never adjacent to an underscore.

## User Impact

Discord reasoning chunks that split at a code fence or inline code boundary now render correctly — no broken fences, no `_``, trailing prose after inline code keeps its italics.

## Evidence

### Production-path proof (3 boundary scenarios)

```
$ node --import tsx -e '...'

=== code fence boundary ===
chunk0: starts="Reasoning:" OK
chunk1: starts="```python" OK

=== inline code boundary ===
chunk0: starts="Reasoning:" OK
chunk1: starts="`inline code` trailing text" OK

=== normal continuation ===
chunk0: reopensItalics=N/A
chunk1: reopensItalics=true first40="_10. normal text\n  11. indented line_"
```

### Tests

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/discord/src/chunk.test.ts
 ✓ 19 passed  (17 existing + 2 new)
```

New assertions in the inline code test:
- `chunks[inlineIdx - 1].trimEnd().endsWith("_")` → `true` (chunk0 closes normally)
- `lines[1].startsWith("_")` → `true` (reopen lands after first line, before trailing prose)

New assertions in the code fence test:
- `chunks[fenceIdx - 1].trimEnd().endsWith("_")` → `false` (close skipped for fence boundary)
- No `_``` ` in any chunk

### Lint + Typecheck

```
$ node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs extensions/discord/src/chunk.ts extensions/discord/src/chunk.test.ts
 exit 0

$ pnpm exec tsgo --project tsconfig.json --noEmit
 (no chunk errors)
```

### Files Changed (2 files, +40/-14)

Production: `startsWithFence` + `startsWithBacktick` helpers, fence-vs-inline branching in reopen. Tests: 2 new assertions for inline code + fence boundary exact-output checks.

No config, SDK, CLI, docs, or changelog surface was added. Bounded to `extensions/discord/src/`.

target.title: fix(terminal): keep C1 CSI and BEL-terminated OSC-8 links intact when wrapping table cells
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`renderTable` uses `wrapLine` to wrap long cell values. `wrapLine` only recognized ANSI sequences that start with `ESC [` (SGR) or `ESC ]8;;` followed by `ESC \\` (OSC-8). This left two gaps:

1. **BEL-terminated OSC-8 links**: `formatTerminalLink` emits OSC-8 hyperlinks terminated by `BEL` (`\x07`). When such a link had to wrap, `wrapLine` treated the introducer and payload as plain characters and split them apart.
2. **C1 CSI / C1 OSC**: Sequences using the 8-bit introducers `\x9b` (C1 CSI) and `\x9d` (C1 OSC) were not recognized as ANSI tokens, so they were split at character boundaries and leaked raw C1/escape bytes into the rendered table.
3. **OSC-8 state at wrap boundaries**: Even after recognizing OSC-8 tokens, an active hyperlink was not closed before a physical line break and reopened on the continuation, so link styling could bleed across padding/separators or unrelated text.

## Why This Change Was Made

Extended `wrapLine` to recognize:
- C1 CSI SGR sequences (`\x9b...m`) in addition to `ESC [...m`.
- BEL-terminated OSC-8 links (`ESC ]8;;...BEL`) in addition to `ESC ]8;;...ESC \\`.
- C1 OSC-8 links (`\x9d8;;...ST`) where the string terminator may be `BEL`, `ESC \\`, or `\x9c`.

Added `parseOsc8Params` and `activeOsc8After` to track active hyperlink state. `flushAt` now closes any open OSC-8 link before the physical line boundary and reopens it on the continuation, matching the existing SGR continuation behavior.

## User Impact

Table cells containing terminal hyperlinks or C1-prefixed ANSI styling now wrap cleanly without corrupting escape sequences, leaking raw control bytes, or letting hyperlink state bleed across unrelated text.

## Real behavior proof

Negative control (origin/main version of `packages/terminal-core/src/table.ts`):

BEL-terminated OSC-8 link forced to wrap:
```text
+------+-------+
| Name | Link  |
+------+-------+
| Plai | \x1b]8;; |
| n    | https |
|      | ://   |
|      | openc |
|      | law.  |
|      | ai\x07Op |
|      | enCla |
|      | w\x1b]8; |
|      | ;\x07    |
+------+-------+
```

C1 CSI SGR forced to wrap:
```text
+-----+
| H   |
+-----+
| \x9b31 |
| mRe |
| d\x9b0 |
| m   |
+-----+
```

Fix applied:

BEL-terminated OSC-8 link:
```text
+------+-------+
| Name | Link  |
+------+-------+
| Plai | \x1b]8;;https://openclaw.ai\x07OpenC\x1b]8;;\x07 |
| n    | \x1b]8;;https://openclaw.ai\x07law\x1b]8;;\x07   |
+------+-------+
```

Embedded OSC-8 link with prefix/suffix (`before ${link} after`) forced to wrap:
```text
+--------------------+
| V                  |
+--------------------+
| before \x1b]8;;https://openclaw.ai\x07Open\x1b]8;;\x07 a |
| fter               |
+--------------------+
```

Note that "after" is no longer inside the hyperlink on the first line.

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/terminal-core` — 12 files, 82 tests passed.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users who cancel a session grep during startup could still have `ripgrep` start after the abort signal was already set.

## Why This Change Was Made

The grep session tool now checks cancellation after resolving `rg` and again at the final pre-spawn boundary after asynchronous search-path validation. This keeps the owner-local startup path aligned with the session search cancellation invariant without changing tool arguments, provider policy, config, or public contracts.

## User Impact

target.title: fix(novita): discover live account model catalog for listing and runtime (#103532)
target.body:
## Summary

The Novita provider plugin only exposed its **static manifest catalog**, so `openclaw models list --provider novita` and runtime model resolution never saw account-available routes (e.g. the reported `novita/deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash`). This PR adds authenticated **live model discovery** — activated through the plugin manifest — with the static catalog kept as an offline/auth-failure fallback.

Fixes #103532.

## What Problem This Solves

After configuring a Novita API key, the model selector stayed empty and a configured model like `novita/deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash` failed at runtime with `Unknown model … no matching models.providers["novita"].models[]`. The shipped plugin returned only fixed manifest rows and never queried the account catalog.

## Root Cause

- `provider-catalog.ts` returned only the static `NOVITA_MODEL_CATALOG`.
- Provider-filtered listing returns manifest rows before consulting a live catalog, and the runtime unknown-model path rejects any model absent from the resolved catalog.
- **Critically**, the Novita manifest did not opt into live discovery, so `catalog.run` / `augmentModelCatalog` hooks stay inert in production (listing returns static rows before `catalog.run`; bundled loading skips `augmentModelCatalog` without `runtimeAugment`).

## Changes

- **`openclaw.plugin.json`**: declare `modelCatalog.runtimeAugment = true` and `discovery.novita = "refreshable"` so provider-filtered listing consults `catalog.run` and bundled loading runs `augmentModelCatalog` (mirrors `chutes` / `anthropic`).
- **`provider-catalog.ts`**: authenticated live discovery via the provider SDK cached live-catalog runtime (`getCachedLiveProviderModelRows`, SSRF-guarded, 5s timeout, 5min TTL). When discovery succeeds, **curated static metadata (reasoning, vision, context, pricing) is preserved for models the manifest already knows**, conservative synthesis is used only for new account-only routes. A custom Novita baseUrl suppresses discovery so the credential is never sent to the public endpoint.
- **`index.test.ts`**: regression coverage for manifest activation, live discovery reaching both listing and runtime-registration paths with a `Bearer` header, and known-vs-new metadata behavior.
- **`docs/providers/novita.md`**: clarify the bundled list is the offline fallback.

## Evidence

**CI:** all required checks green (types, lint, extension-package-boundary, extension-bundled, test shards).

**Credentialed live proof (real Novita API key, redacted `sk_***…*** (46 chars)`)** — driving the **real** `buildNovitaProvider` against the **real** `https://api.novita.ai/openai/v1/models` endpoint:

```
=== static fallback catalog ===
count: 6

=== LIVE account catalog (real Novita /models) ===
count: 139
discovery active (differs from static): true
includes reported model 'deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash': true
account-only routes not in static (sample): baidu/ernie-4.5-300b-a47b-paddle,
  baidu/ernie-4.5-vl-424b-a47b, deepseek/deepseek_v3, deepseek/deepseek-ocr, ...
known model kimi-k2.5 kept curated metadata:
  {"reasoning":true,"input":["text","image"],"contextWindow":262144}
```

This confirms provider-filtered listing surfaces account-only routes (incl. the reported `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash`), and that curated metadata for known models survives the sparse live rows.

**Runtime turn:** a live chat completion returned `HTTP 403 {"reason":"NOT_ENOUGH_BALANCE"}` for every model (including known static routes) — the test account has no inference credit, so a completion cannot be demonstrated with this key. This is an account-balance limitation, not a code issue; the discovery/listing/registration path is fully exercised above.

target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`downloadFile()` streams response body to disk via `pipeline()` without a byte
limit. A hostile server can send unbounded data, exhausting disk space.

## Why This Change Was Made

Added `SKILL_DOWNLOAD_MAX_BYTES` (100 MiB) enforced via a Transform stream
counter inside the pipeline. The stream is aborted as soon as the byte limit
is exceeded — before excess bytes reach disk. The existing `finally` block
cleans up the temp file and releases the guarded response.

## User Impact

**Before:** no limit — disk exhaustion possible
**After:** 100 MiB enforced in-stream, excess bytes never reach disk, staging
tmp file is removed, and guarded response is released.

## Evidence

Branch: `fix/install-download-maxbytes` | Base: `upstream/main` | Node: v22.19.0 — linux

### Real behavior proof

Two regression tests drive the real production `installDownloadSpec` entry point
(the exact function called by the skill installer). The HTTP layer is mocked
but the full production download pipeline — Transform counter, file write,

target.title: fix: strip volatile output from exec result hash to fix no-progress detection (#93917)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where repeated failed `exec` calls never triggered the no-progress
circuit breaker when the error output text varied across calls. This happens
commonly with command-not-found, timeouts, and killed processes whose error
message carries fresh timestamps, PIDs, or session ids each retry while the
actual failure mode is identical.

Fixes #93917

## Why This Change Was Made

`hashExecToolOutcome` is split so a `failed` exec result is hashed without its
volatile output text, while a `completed` result keeps output in the hash as a
real progress signal. Failed retries are instead compared by stable failure
metadata (`status`, `exitCode`, `timedOut`, `exitSignal`, `failureKind`), so
identical failures with different error strings still count as no progress.

The production foreground exec path now carries those stable discriminators end
to end: `ExecToolDetails` (and `buildExecForegroundResult` plus the node-host and
gateway producers) propagate `failureKind` and `exitSignal`, tightened to
`ExecToolFailureKind`, so the hash receives real values at runtime instead of
`null`. This addresses @vincentkoc's blocking finding that the discriminators
were absent on the real result.

## User Impact

Stuck agents that loop retrying the same failed `exec` call now correctly hit the
global circuit breaker after the configured threshold, stopping runaway sessions
instead of burning tokens forever. Genuinely different failure modes stay
distinct and are not merged.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `bash-tools.exec-types.ts` | Add `ExecToolFailureKind`; `failed` `ExecToolDetails` carries `exitSignal` + `failureKind` |
| `bash-tools.exec-host-node-phases.ts`, `bash-tools.exec-runtime.ts`, `bash-tools.exec-host-gateway.ts` | Propagate stable failure fields through the real foreground producers |
| `tool-loop-detection.ts` | Split `hashExecToolOutcome`: `completed` keeps output; `failed` strips output, keeps `{status,exitCode,timedOut,exitSignal,failureKind}` |
| `tool-loop-detection.exec-foreground.test.ts` | **Real foreground exec** regression test through the production tool path |
| `tool-loop-detection.test.ts` | Unit coverage for failure-kind / exitSignal distinctness |
| `docs/tools/loop-detection.md` | Document the completed-vs-failed outcome equivalence rule |

## Evidence

### Real foreground exec proof (production tool path, no hand-built details)

`tool-loop-detection.exec-foreground.test.ts` drives the actual exec tool
(`createOpenClawCodingTools` -> `execTool.execute`) against a command that fails
with volatile stderr but identical params, then feeds each real result through
the production recorders (`recordToolCall` / `recordToolCallOutcome`) and
`detectToolCallLoop`.

The real foreground failed result (captured at exact head) carries the stable
discriminators — not manufactured values:

```
first failed details: {"status":"failed","exitCode":127,"exitSignal":null,"failureKind":"shell-command-not-found"}
breaker: {"stuck":true,"level":"critical","detector":"global_circuit_breaker","count":4,
          "warningKey":"global:exec:...:bed082ca..."}   # identical outcome hash across 4 varying-stderr calls
distinct: {"notFound":"shell-command-not-found","notFoundExit":127,
           "timedOut":"overall-timeout","timedOutSignal":"SIGTERM"}
```

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/tool-loop-detection.exec-foreground.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  2 passed (2)
```

- A real `status:"failed"` foreground exec result carries `failureKind` +
  `exitSignal` into the hash (runtime contract, not unit-only).
- Repeated identical failures with varying stderr trip `global_circuit_breaker`.
- Two genuinely different real failure modes (`shell-command-not-found` vs
  `overall-timeout`) keep distinct fingerprints and do not merge.

### Mutation proof — the fix is what trips the breaker

Reverting only the `failed` branch of `hashExecToolOutcome` to include the
volatile output text (the pre-fix behavior) makes the same real-foreground test
fail, because varying stderr yields a fresh hash each call so the streak never
accumulates:

```
 × trips the no-progress breaker on repeated failed exec with volatile stderr
 AssertionError: expected undefined to be 'global_circuit_breaker'
```

Restoring the fix returns the test to green.

### Unit + regression suites

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/tool-loop-detection.test.ts src/agents/tool-loop-detection.exec-foreground.test.ts
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  60 passed (60)
```

### Maintainer decision still needed

This intentionally changes when failed retries count as no progress (stable
failure metadata now outweighs varying error text). Whether repeated failed exec
with the same stable fingerprint should trip critical/global blocking is a policy
call owned by the assigned reviewer (@vincentkoc). The code, docs, and
exact-head real-foreground proof are in place for that decision.

The Nostr outbound adapter (`extensions/nostr/src/gateway.ts:nostrOutboundAdapter`) had no `sanitizeText` hook. Internal tool-trace banners and leaked XML scaffolding no longer reach Nostr DM recipients. Ordinary assistant prose is preserved unchanged.

N/A (no existing issue). Sibling fixes: #103109, #98693, #98705.
